points.quote: Edgeless mode doesn't store a separate copy of the document. It adds data to the same Yjs doc that page mode uses. ... Edgeless mode reuses it.
The `affine:surface` block is the page's second child. It is the edgeless layer, and its schema declares `parent: ['@root']`.
Shapes, brush strokes, highlighter strokes, connectors, groups, mindmaps and canvas text are not blocks. They live inside the surface block's single `elements` prop.
The page-mode block tree is `affine:page` → `affine:note` blocks → paragraphs, lists and so on. Edgeless mode reuses it. ... This is how a note appears as a card on the canvas.
Rich objects are real child blocks of the surface: `affine:frame`, `affine:image`, `affine:bookmark`, `affine:attachment`, `affine:embed-*` and `affine:edgeless-text`.
**Position:** every element and every edgeless block has `xywh`. It is a serialized string such as `"[x,y,w,h]"`.

**Stacking:** each element and block has a fractional-indexing string in `index`, generated with `generateKeyBetween`. ... `blocksuite/framework/std/src/gfx/layer.ts` sorts by this string to produce the z-order.

**Grouping:** a `group` element ... has a `children` prop that is a `Y.Map<boolean>` of child id → `true`, plus a `title` Y.Text. A child can be an element or a block, and the group's bounds come from them.
